Variable_Definitions: R_compute_required = required average operations per second; W = total workload operations/work; T_target = target execution time

Source_Type: Derived from source-supported work/time performance relationship
Applicability: Only when workload work W and target time are explicitly defined or reliably measured
Limitations: Not a universal FLOPs/model formula; does not predict achieved application throughput from peak TFLOPS and ignores memory, overhead, utilization, synchronization, and software effects. Must not be used as TFLOPS-to-tokens/s conversion.

Formula_Name: Weight Memory From Parameter Count and Stored Representation
Variable_Definitions: P = number of stored model parameters; B = bytes used by the actual stored weight representation per parameter; M_weight = weight memory
Inputs: Model parameter count and actual weight-storage representation
Page_Section_Equation: NVIDIA NIM LLM Memory Troubleshooting — How GPU Memory Is Used / weight memory
Source_Type: Source-supported relationship; NVIDIA also presents a per-GPU heuristic when parallelization is explicitly configured.
Applicability: Applicable when the representation can be represented by a defined bytes-per-parameter value.
Limitations: Do not assume B from compute precision alone. Quantization metadata, scaling factors, duplicated higher-precision copies and runtime transformations may add memory. No GPU-count formula is included in Part 2.

Formula: M_train = M_weights + M_gradients + M_optimizer + M_activations + M_runtime
Variables: M_train; M_weights; M_gradients; M_optimizer; M_activations; M_runtime
Variable_Definitions: Each term is the applicable peak/resident memory component for the selected training configuration.
Output: Total applicable training GPU memory requirement
Page_Section_Equation: PyTorch training memory components; Megatron Bridge theoretical memory estimator
Source_Type: Derived from multiple authoritative descriptions of distinct training memory components.
Applicability: This is an accounting identity/methodology, not a universal multiplier. Some components may be zero/not applicable; peak overlap/liveness must be modeled when components coexist. Exact activation/runtime estimation is configuration-dependent.

Formula: M_KV = 2 × B_req × L × H_KV × D_head × S × B_elem
Variables: M_KV; B_req; L; H_KV; D_head; S; B_elem
Variable_Definitions: B_req = number of concurrent requests/sequences represented in the cache; L = number of attention layers; H_KV = number of KV heads; D_head = head dimension; S = cached sequence/context tokens; B_elem = bytes per KV element; 2 = K and V
Units: bytes; requests; layers; heads; elements; tokens; bytes/element
Inputs: Autoregressive transformer using explicit KV caching with the stated attention geometry
Page_Section_Equation: Hugging Face — Unlocking Longer Generation with KV Cache Quantization; TensorRT-LLM Memory Usage
Source_Type: Source-supported architecture relationship; TensorRT-LLM separately documents runtime allocation and batch/sequence dependence.
Applicability: Exact runtime implementations may use GQA/MQA, paging, sliding windows, quantization, prefix reuse, offloading or other mechanisms. H_KV must be the actual KV-head count, not blindly the query-head count. This formula is not applicable to non-KV-cache architectures without modification.

Variable_Definitions: Applicable static and dynamic inference memory components for the selected runtime.
Output: Total applicable inference GPU memory requirement
Page_Section_Equation: TensorRT-LLM Memory Usage — inference-time GPU memory contributors
Source_Type: Derived accounting relation from NVIDIA's identified major inference memory contributors.
Applicability: Not every inference workload uses a KV cache. Runtime may use additional buffers, graphs or workspace. Components can have different peak-liveness relationships, so a simple sum may be conservative unless peak overlap is modeled.

Variable_Definitions: M_required_applicable = configuration-derived memory requirement within the same scope; M_candidate_applicable = candidate capacity within the same hardware/entity scope.
Inputs: Aligned workload requirement and candidate capacity
Page_Section_Equation: DSS GPU Hardware Catalogue; TensorRT-LLM Memory Usage
Source_Type: Derived feasibility comparison from capacity and requirement definitions.
Applicability: No universal safety margin is inserted. Candidate capacity may be physical rather than usable; if usable-memory evidence is material, the comparison remains insufficient until that distinction is resolved. Aggregate memory cannot substitute for per-accelerator capacity.

Page_Section_Equation: Scaling efficiency analysis; no universal threshold

Formula_Name: Training Time Under Observed Scaling Efficiency
Variable_Definitions: T(N) = estimated/observed training time at N GPUs; T(1) = baseline training time; N = GPU count; E(N) = observed or externally validated scaling efficiency
Inputs: Comparable baseline time, candidate GPU count and validated efficiency
Applicability: Only where E(N) is measured/validated for the same workload/configuration or a justified comparable case
Limitations: Never assume E(N)=1; extrapolation beyond measured N requires additional evidence.

Formula_Name: Preliminary Inference GPU Count Lower Bound From Throughput
Variable_Definitions: N_lower_bound = preliminary GPU/entity count; R_required = target request/token throughput; R_1 = measured single-GPU throughput under the same serving configuration
Units: count; requests/s or tokens/s; same throughput unit

Applicability: Throughput-oriented inference only when single-GPU throughput is measured comparably
Limitations: Not valid as a latency sizing rule; ignores non-linear multi-GPU scaling until validated at candidate counts.

Variable_Definitions: N = candidate GPU/entity count; R(N) = measured throughput at N; R_required = target throughput; L(N) = measured latency at N under target load; L_target = latency target

Limitations: Requires measured R(N) and L(N); no universal scaling curve or latency model is assumed.
